name: MAX481ESA+T
title: MAX481/MAX483/MAX485/MAX487-MAX491/MAX1487: RS-485/RS-422 transceivers, low power, with optional slew-rate limiting
summary: A family of nine 5 V RS-485/RS-422 transceivers, each one driver plus one receiver. Five are half duplex on one pair (MAX481, MAX483, MAX485, MAX487, MAX1487) and four full duplex on two pairs (MAX488 to MAX491). The fast parts run to 2.5 Mbps; MAX483 and MAX487 to MAX489 limit their slew rate for low EMI and run to 250 kbps. MAX487 and MAX1487 are quarter-unit-load (128 per bus), MAX481/MAX483/MAX487 can shut down to 0.1 µA, and every driver is current-limited with thermal shutdown.

circuits.title: Figure 21. MAX481/MAX483/MAX485/MAX487/MAX1487 typical half-duplex RS-485 network
circuits.description: Four half-duplex transceivers hang off one bus pair, A and B. The two ends of the bus each carry a 120 Ω resistor across the pair; the two middle nodes tap the pair without termination. Every node has its own DI, DE, RO and RE lines.
notes: All parts run from a single 5 V supply.

circuits.title: Figure 22. MAX488-MAX491 full-duplex RS-485 network
circuits.description: Four full-duplex transceivers on two bus pairs. U1 at the left end drives one pair (Z, Y) and listens on the other (A, B); U2 at the right end and the two middle nodes drive the pair U1 listens on and listen on the pair U1 drives. Both pairs are terminated with 120 Ω at each end; the middle nodes are unterminated taps.
notes: RE and DE exist on the MAX489/MAX491 only.
All parts run from a single 5 V supply.

circuits.title: Figure 23. Line repeater for MAX488-MAX491
circuits.description: One full-duplex transceiver regenerates a line: the incoming pair, terminated in 120 Ω, enters A and B; RO is wired straight to DI; Y and Z drive the outgoing pair, which also has 120 Ω across it. This carries a link past the 4000-foot reach of one cable run.
notes: RE and DE exist on the MAX489/MAX491 only.

operation.text: Nine 5 V RS-485/RS-422 transceivers, each with one line driver and one line receiver. MAX481, MAX483, MAX485, MAX487 and MAX1487 put driver and receiver on one bus pair (half duplex); MAX488 to MAX491 give each its own pair (full duplex). All run from a single 5 V supply.

MAX481, MAX485, MAX490, MAX491 and MAX1487 have unlimited driver edges and run to 2.5 Mbps. MAX483, MAX487, MAX488 and MAX489 slow their driver edges, which cuts EMI and reflections from poorly terminated cable, and are specified to 250 kbps.
Unloaded, or loaded with the driver disabled, the parts draw 120 µA to 500 µA. MAX481, MAX483 and MAX487 add a shutdown mode drawing 0.1 µA typical.

MAX481, MAX483, MAX485, MAX487, MAX489, MAX491 and MAX1487 have DE (driver enable) and RE (receiver enable, active low). A disabled driver or receiver output is high impedance. MAX488 and MAX490 have no enables: the driver and receiver are always on.

Standard parts (MAX481, MAX483, MAX485, MAX488 to MAX491) present a 12 kΩ receiver input, one unit load, so 32 can share a bus. MAX487 and MAX1487 present 48 kΩ, a quarter unit load, so 128 can share a bus. Any mix is allowed as long as the total stays at 32 unit loads or fewer.
With the receiver inputs open, RO is guaranteed high.

Shutdown happens only when both halves are off: RE high and DE low. Supply current then falls to 0.1 µA typical. RE and DE can switch at the same moment: a state shorter than 50 ns never causes shutdown, and one lasting 600 ns or more always does. Waking from shutdown takes longer than enabling from the operating mode, so tZH(SHDN) and tZL(SHDN) apply after shutdown and tZH and tZL otherwise. The part is in operating mode for (RE, DE) = (0, 1), (1, 1) or (0, 0). MAX485, MAX488 to MAX491 and MAX1487 have no shutdown.

A foldback current limit in the output stage guards against shorts at once, anywhere across the common-mode range. A thermal shutdown circuit puts the driver outputs into high impedance if the die gets too hot. Together they handle faults and bus contention.

Receiver delay difference |tPLH - tPHL| is typically below 13 ns on MAX481, MAX485, MAX490, MAX491 and MAX1487, and below 100 ns on MAX483 and MAX487 to MAX489. Driver skew is 5 ns typical and 10 ns maximum on the fast parts, 100 ns typical and 800 ns maximum on the slew-limited parts. This matters to encoding schemes that rely on matched driver and receiver delays.
The RS-485/RS-422 standard covers runs up to 4000 feet. Longer runs use the transceivers as line repeaters (Figure 23).

Each end of the line gets a termination equal to the cable's characteristic impedance, and stubs off the main line are kept as short as possible. The slew-limited MAX483 and MAX487 to MAX489 tolerate imperfect termination better.

Sending a 150 kHz signal, the fast parts (MAX481, MAX485, MAX490, MAX491, MAX1487) show large high-frequency harmonics in the output spectrum; the slew-limited parts (MAX483, MAX487 to MAX489) show much smaller ones, so less EMI. The spectra span 0 Hz to 5 MHz at 500 kHz/div and 10 dB/div (Figures 12 and 13).

Measured in the Figure 14 circuit at VCC = 5 V, TA = +25 °C: Figures 15 and 16 show receiver tPHL and tPLH for MAX481/MAX485/MAX490/MAX491/MAX1487 at 20 ns/div; Figures 17 and 18 show them for MAX483 and MAX487 to MAX489 at 400 ns/div. A and B are at 500 mV/div, RO at 2 V/div.

DI, DE and RE switch between 0 V and 3 V and are timed at 1.5 V. Driver delays are timed at half the output swing; driver rise and fall at 10 % and 90 % of the differential swing. Driver enable times are taken at 2.3 V on the output, receiver enable times at 1.5 V. Disable times end when the output has moved 0.5 V from VOL or VOH. Receiver delays run from the 0 V crossing of A - B to 1.5 V on RO.
On the half-duplex parts, the timing, test and waveform figures call the driver outputs Y and Z; with DE high these are pins A and B.
For isolated links, the MAX253 and MAX1480 are the companion parts.
